title: Abhidhammattha-saṅgaha Library
tagline: Ācariya Anuruddha’s manual of the Abhidhamma — its Pāli text, its commentaries and its translations — one chapter per page, with the Saṅgaha’s own paragraphs as a common map between the books.

books.title: Buddha Abhidhamma: Ultimate Science
books.author: Dr. Mehm Tin Mon
books.by: Dr. Mehm Tin Mon, Saddhamma Jotikadhaja · Buddha Dharma Education Association Inc. (BuddhaNet)
books.blurb: A whole course on the Saṅgaha by a Myanmar Abhidhamma teacher: the nine chapters explained with tables, symbols and reviews, from the 89 cittas to the stages of insight.
books.note: The whole book, one chapter per page: the Preface and Introduction, the nine chapters, which are the Saṅgaha’s own (each linked to the same chapter in the other books on the Saṅgaha map), and the Conclusion. The book’s tables are kept with their columns. The charts it refers to as “attached at the back” (Charts 1–10) are not in this PDF.
books.toc_foot: The nine chapters of the Saṅgaha, with the Preface and the Conclusion.
books.source: Source: Dr. Mehm Tin Mon, Buddha Abhidhamma: Ultimate Science, Buddha Dharma Education Association Inc. (BuddhaNet), from the PDF (PageMaker, 2003), taken from its text layer. The PDF is set in an old Pāli font that puts accented letters for the Pāli ones (à for ā, ñ for ṭ, ü for ṃ …); these are turned into the Pāli letters throughout. Line-end hyphens are joined. The charts at the back of the printed book are not in the PDF.
books.desc: Dr. Mehm Tin Mon’s Buddha Abhidhamma: Ultimate Science, a course on the nine chapters of the Abhidhammatthasaṅgaha.

books.title: Fundamental Abhidhamma, Part I
books.author: Dr. Nandamālābhivaṃsa
books.edition: Centre for Buddhist Studies, Sagaing, 2nd ed. 2005
books.by: Dr. Ashin Nandamālābhivaṃsa, Sagaing Hills · Centre for Buddhist Studies (CBS), Mahāsubodhayon Monastery, Sagaing, Myanmar
books.blurb: A compact course from a Sagaing teacher: the history of the Abhidhamma, then citta, cetasika, rūpa, the miscellaneous section and the cognitive process, in tables.
books.note: Part I, one chapter per page: the Editorial Preface, About the Author and The History of Abhidhamma, then the five chapters of Part I. Its chapters are in its own order — 1 Citta, 2 Cetasika, 3 Rūpa (the Saṅgaha’s chapter VI), 4 Pakiṇṇaka (III), 5 Vīthi (IV) — and the Saṅgaha map links each to the Saṅgaha’s chapter. Part II (from Vīthi on) is in a second copy whose text layer is unreadable; it waits for OCR.
books.toc_foot: Part I: five chapters, with the history of the Abhidhamma.
books.source: Source: Dr. Nandamālābhivaṃsa, Fundamental Abhidhamma, Part I, 2nd extended edition, January 2005, revised November 2005, © Centre for Buddhist Studies, Sagaing, from the PDF (Acrobat from Word, 2006), taken from its text layer. The tables are kept with their columns.
books.desc: Dr. Nandamālābhivaṃsa’s Fundamental Abhidhamma, Part I: citta, cetasika, rūpa, the miscellaneous section and the cognitive process.

books.title: Abhidhammatthasaṅgaho
books.author: Ācariya Anuruddha
books.edition: Sixth Council edition, VRI digital text
books.by: Ācariya Anuruddha · the Sixth Council (Chaṭṭha Saṅgāyana) text, Yangon · digital edition of the Vipassana Research Institute
books.blurb: The manual itself: the four ultimate realities in nine chapters, from consciousness to meditation, in verse and prose.
books.note: The whole text, one chapter per page: the opening verses, the nine paricchedas and the closing verses. Each paragraph carries the Saṅgaha’s own number (I.1, I.2 … IX.75), the map that every book of this library follows; a small chip beside it opens the same paragraph in the Vibhāvinī. The pages of the Myanmar edition are marked in the margin.
books.toc_foot: The nine chapters ({{NPARA}} numbered paragraphs), in the Sixth Council text.
books.source: Source: the Chaṭṭha Saṅgāyana (Sixth Council) text as published in digital form by the Vipassana Research Institute (github.com/VipassanaTech/tipitaka-xml), file romn/abh07t.nrf.xml, first book. The text is unchanged; the paragraph numbers and the Myanmar edition’s page numbers are as in the file. In Chapter IV the file numbers its paragraphs 1, 2, 4 (there is no 3); the numbers are kept as they are.
books.desc: The Abhidhammatthasaṅgaha in the Pāli of the Sixth Council edition, with its paragraph numbers, linked to its commentaries and translations.
howto: Type in Search (or press /). Accents are optional: rupa finds rūpa.
Type chapter and paragraph in §, e.g. 4.6 for IV.6.
The chip beside a paragraph opens the same paragraph in the Vibhāvinī.

books.title: A Manual of Abhidhamma
books.author: Nārada Thera
books.edition: Vājirārāma, Colombo; Preface dated 1978; palikanon.com web edition
books.by: Abhidhammattha-Saṅgaha of Anuruddhācariya, edited in the original Pāli text with English translation and explanatory notes by Nārada Thera, Vājirārāma, Colombo
books.blurb: The Saṅgaha section by section: Nārada’s Pāli, his English, and his explanatory notes, with diagrams.
books.note: Chapters I–VII and IX, one per page, after the Preface. Nārada numbers his sections § 1, § 2 … in each chapter; a chip beside a section opens the same Pāli in the Sixth Council Saṅgaha and the Vibhāvinī. Chapter VIII (Paccaya) is missing from this copy: its contents list it, but the text runs from Chapter VII to Chapter IX.
books.toc_foot: Chapters I–VII and IX ({{NPARA}} sections); Chapter VIII is missing from this copy.
books.source: Source: Nārada Thera, Abhidhammattha-Sangaha of Anuruddhācariya: A Manual of Abhidhamma, Vājirārāma, Colombo, from the web edition of palikanon.com as a PDF (Word, 2010; “for free distribution only”). The text is taken as it is in the PDF, whose Pāli writes plain m and n for ṃ and ṅ; the diagrams are its text tables, shown with their columns as the PDF has them (some cells are broken over two lines there).
books.desc: Nārada Thera’s Manual of Abhidhamma: the Abhidhammatthasaṅgaha in Pāli and English with explanatory notes, linked to the Pāli text.

books.title: Abhidhammatthavibhāvinīṭīkā
books.author: Ācariya Sumaṅgala
books.edition: Sixth Council edition, VRI digital text
books.by: Ācariya Sumaṅgala (12th century) · the Sixth Council text · digital edition of the Vipassana Research Institute
books.blurb: The classic commentary on the Saṅgaha, read in Myanmar beside the root text; explains it phrase by phrase.
books.note: The whole commentary, one chapter per page. VRI numbers it by the paragraph of the Saṅgaha it explains, so each numbered paragraph carries that Saṅgaha number (I.11 …) and a chip back to it. The words of the Saṅgaha being explained are in bold, as in the edition.
books.toc_foot: The commentary on the nine chapters ({{NPARA}} numbered paragraphs).
books.source: Source: the Chaṭṭha Saṅgāyana (Sixth Council) text as published in digital form by the Vipassana Research Institute (github.com/VipassanaTech/tipitaka-xml), file romn/abh07t.nrf.xml, second book (Abhidhammatthavibhāvinīṭīkā). The text is unchanged; the closing verses (Nigamanakathā) keep their own numbers 1–7 in the text.
books.desc: The Abhidhammatthavibhāvinī-ṭīkā in Pāli, paragraph by paragraph against the Abhidhammatthasaṅgaha.

books.title: Paramatthadīpanī
books.author: Ledi Sayadaw
books.edition: Sixth Council edition, VRI digital text
books.by: Ledi Sayadaw (1846–1923) · Saṅgaha-mahāṭīkā · digital edition of the Vipassana Research Institute
books.blurb: Ledi Sayadaw’s great commentary on the Saṅgaha, which weighs the Vibhāvinī and often disagrees with it.
books.note: The whole text, one chapter of the Saṅgaha per page, with its own paragraph numbers (1–174) running through the book; a chip beside each opens the same paragraph in the Anudīpanī, Ledi Sayadaw’s own commentary on it.
books.source: Source: the Chaṭṭha Saṅgāyana (Sixth Council) text as published in digital form by the Vipassana Research Institute (github.com/VipassanaTech/tipitaka-xml), file romn/e0301n.nrf.xml. The text is unchanged. Where the file repeats a paragraph number (66, 67) or prints one out of order (31), the number is left in the text as printed and not made an anchor.
books.desc: Ledi Sayadaw’s Paramatthadīpanī on the Abhidhammatthasaṅgaha, in Pāli.
